page: Google Cloud Platform a3-ultragpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized server designed for massive parallel computing workloads. It features eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs from the Hopper architecture, providing a total of 1128 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with 224 vCPUs (112 physical cores) running at 2.1 GHz, supported by 2952.0 GB of system memory. This configuration does not include local SSD storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU capabilities, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core performance and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read-only small block bandwidth and uncached large block read/write speeds both ranking in the top 10%. The system also excels in specialized tasks, achieving top-tier results in Geekbench software compiling, ray tracing, and image processing, alongside strong performance in text processing and database operations.

While the server offers immense computational density and memory capacity, the complete absence of local SSD storage requires external storage solutions for data persistence. The high-density hardware profile represents a significant resource commitment, making it highly cost-efficient for large-scale AI training, complex LLM inference, high-performance computing (HPC), and advanced data science workloads, but less suitable for general-purpose tasks that do not leverage its massive GPU and memory resources.
